items.title: Pug Horton interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 22, 1998
items.q: we were starting to have these bands sprouting up... everybody was mad to play like all of these bands that they had heard... some of them, like Monty Sunshine or Chris Barber, Ken Collier, did form bands and did become quite successful

ctx.x: So did you need to search out other musicians a few years later, so that you could get to sing?

No because suddenly, don’t forget this was getting into the late 40s, and just after the war, and we were starting to have these bands sprouting up, all having listened to records and not always the best records because we had this rose thorn don’t forget that took a lot away from the fidelity, and so everybody was mad to play like all of these bands that they had heard. So there was a lot of opportunity to sing around with mostly university students who subsequently either went on to become doctors, lawyers or…
Do you recall some of the first tunes that you sang with these bands?
